criteria.fidelity: Reproduces every stateAndScoreInputs item of the baseline and passes its referenceCases.
criteria.interaction: Touch, swipe, keyboard, D-pad, mouse and watch input reach the same four moves plus skip and restart.
criteria.distribution: A store or channel can carry it and an update can be held and released on a chosen date.
criteria.online: Can submit a run to one shared leaderboard keyed by game type and content version.

evidence.finding: KMP: Android and JVM desktop Stable; Web on Kotlin/JS Stable; Web on Kotlin/Wasm Beta.
Compose Multiplatform for Web (Wasm) is Beta; no Stable announcement found.
Compose Desktop packages Windows EXE/MSI via jpackage, built on a Windows host; no built-in MSIX and no built-in auto-update.
MSIX can be produced from an MSI with the MSIX Packaging Tool or by makeappx over the distributable folder.
A standalone Wear OS app declares com.google.android.wearable.standalone=true and needs no phone app for core features.
Wear APKs/AABs are uploaded and updated independently of phone ones in Play Console; listing must name Wear OS and carry a watch screenshot; 64-bit required since 2026-09-15.
Play Games Services leaderboards exist with a REST surface (games.googleapis.com); identity is a Play Games / Google account.
PGS REST: list leaderboards, submit scores; non-Android use needs OAuth - not confirmed for Windows or Web in this pass.
Board identity depends on kotlin.random.Random's exact sequence.
The two in-repo copies of the rules already drift in board generation.

dependencies: new applicationId (frozen at Play console creation)
platforms.tradeOffs: Direct reuse of app_v2 game code; View/XML today, Compose possible.
platforms.parityCheck: Run all baseline referenceCases as JVM unit tests on the shared core.

platforms.tradeOffs: Existing Compose watch UI; board geometry is round (WD-02), which affects ranked parity.
platforms.parityCheck: Same referenceCases on the shared core; geometry cases per Q-PAR-01.

platforms.tradeOffs: Compose Desktop on JVM reuses Kotlin core as-is; runtime adds size; MSIX needs extra tooling. A native C# shell would need a ported rules core.
platforms.parityCheck: Same JVM tests run unchanged on the desktop target.

platforms.tradeOffs: Kotlin/JS core is Stable; Compose Web UI is Beta. A hand-written JS port breaks seed portability (EV-09). Web is also the only channel with no store review delay.
platforms.parityCheck: KMP common tests executed on the js target; golden board RC-GEN-05.

codeSharing.requirement: One canonical rules, generator and scoring source
codeSharing.description: Kotlin Multiplatform common module holding the domain (models, generator, rules, scoring, snapshot); each platform keeps a native shell (Views or Compose on Android, Compose on Wear, Compose Desktop, Compose Web or a JS/HTML canvas).
dependencies: PRNG must be specified and implemented in common code, not kotlin.random default, if non-JVM targets must agree
codeSharing.tradeOffs: Lowest drift; UI written per platform; FMS_A could later consume the same module.
codeSharing.fmsAChange: Optional: FMS_A switching to the shared module touches app_v2 and wear game packages - owner approval Q-DEV-04.
codeSharing.parityCheck: commonTest runs the baseline referenceCases on every target.

codeSharing.description: Compose Multiplatform UI shared across Android, Desktop, Web; Wear keeps a Compose for Wear shell over the same drawing code.
codeSharing.tradeOffs: One renderer means visual parity for free; Web target maturity risk; watch layout still separate.
codeSharing.parityCheck: Screenshot comparison per mode per platform.

codeSharing.description: Rewrite in a game engine (Godot, Unity) exporting to all targets.
dependencies: full rewrite of rules in another language
engine export to Wear is not a supported path
codeSharing.tradeOffs: Rich effects, but breaks 'first version = FMS_A code' and seed portability; no Wear export.
codeSharing.parityCheck: Port must pass referenceCases through a cross-language harness.

codeSharing.description: Separate code per platform (Kotlin, C#, TypeScript) kept equal by hand.
codeSharing.tradeOffs: Already drifting with two Kotlin copies; four copies multiply it.
codeSharing.parityCheck: Golden vectors from the baseline replayed per language.

resourceSharing.requirement: Graphics, strings and mods appear everywhere at once
resourceSharing.description: One asset/content folder (vector art as SVG source, strings as one table, mods as data) with a generator emitting Android drawables/strings and desktop/web resources.
resourceSharing.tradeOffs: Needs a converter; Android VectorDrawable is the current source format.
resourceSharing.parityCheck: Content manifest hash equal across builds of one release.

resourceSharing.description: Each platform keeps its resources, synchronized by a script.
resourceSharing.tradeOffs: Simple start, drift risk as in EV-10.

repositoryLayout.description: One new repository with modules core/, android/, wear/, desktop/, web/, content/.
repositoryLayout.tradeOffs: One version, one CI, atomic changes; one release pipeline for four channels.

repositoryLayout.description: Core published as a versioned package; one repository per platform pins a core version.
repositoryLayout.tradeOffs: Per-repo freedom; version skew between platforms becomes possible, which conflicts with 'everything at once'.

repositoryLayout.description: Canonical code copied into each project by a sync script.

repositoryLayout.tradeOffs: Ties game release cadence to FMS_A; FMS repo already has eight flavors.

coordinatedRelease.requirement: Rules, graphics, mods are identical across clients
coordinatedRelease.description: Every build carries rulesVersion and contentVersion; a run records both.
coordinatedRelease.tradeOffs: Required by ranked play regardless of layout.

coordinatedRelease.requirement: Simultaneous availability despite different review times
coordinatedRelease.description: Submit early to every store, hold publication (Play managed publishing, Microsoft Store manual release after certification), release all on one date; Web deploys last.
coordinatedRelease.tradeOffs: Ties release day to the slowest review.

coordinatedRelease.description: Ship new content dark; activate by a server flag once every channel has it.
coordinatedRelease.tradeOffs: Needs the online service; offline clients activate later; mods as data only, never code.

coordinatedRelease.description: Server accepts ranked runs only for active rulesVersion values; an older client plays unranked and is told to update; rollback = re-activate the previous version.
coordinatedRelease.tradeOffs: Clear fairness; may annoy players on slow stores.

sharedRankings.requirement: One top per unique game type across all platforms
sharedRankings.description: Own small backend: issues seeds, accepts a move log, replays it with the shared core to compute the score; key = gameType + rulesVersion (+ contentVersion when it changes rules).
dependencies: privacy page and store data-safety forms change, because run data leaves the device
sharedRankings.tradeOffs: Full control and cheat resistance by server replay; owner operates it.
No server to run; Windows and Web use not confirmed; scores are client-submitted, no replay validation.

sharedRankings.description: A hosted backend (Firebase, Supabase or similar) with a server function replaying runs.
sharedRankings.tradeOffs: Less ops; vendor lock-in and data-processing disclosures.

sharedRankings.description: gameType defined by board geometry, size rule, shadow rule and rulesVersion; today phone and watch would be two game types (WD-02, WD-03, WD-05).
sharedRankings.tradeOffs: Either unify geometry or keep one board per type.
